Ichnya Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Ichnya's earliest evidence of a Jewish community dates to the latter half of the 19th century; Jews were formally granted permission to settle in 1903, and by 1910 the town had 575 Jewish residents, a synagogue, and this cemetery, with Chaim Alexander-Sender Belinka serving as rabbi. The community survived a 1919 pogrom carried out by the Directorate, though its population had fallen to just 148 by 1939. The cemetery has separate sections for men and women; the last known Hasidic Jewish burial took place in 1989.
